latest_nl_proof:
Assume that f has the stated property, let G be any point of R^2, let s>0, and let X,Y,Z be distinct points with ||X-G||=||Y-G||=||Z-G||=s. Assume also that f(X)=f(Y)=f(Z). We must show f(G)=f(X).

First, X,Y,Z are noncollinear. Indeed, they all lie on the circle centered at G with radius s>0. A line can intersect a nondegenerate circle in at most two points, so three distinct points on that circle cannot be collinear.

Next, G is the circumcenter of X,Y,Z. Since ||X-G||=||Y-G||, the point G is equidistant from X and Y, hence G lies on the perpendicular bisector of XY. Likewise, since ||X-G||=||Z-G||, the point G lies on the perpendicular bisector of XZ. Because X,Y,Z are noncollinear, the circumcenter circumcenter(X,Y,Z) is the unique intersection point of these two perpendicular bisectors. Therefore circumcenter(X,Y,Z)=G.

Now we can apply the hypothesis on f to the noncollinear triple X,Y,Z. Since f(X)=f(Y)=f(Z), the hypothesis gives
f(circumcenter(X,Y,Z))=f(X).
Using circumcenter(X,Y,Z)=G, this becomes f(G)=f(X), as required.

So whenever X,Y,Z are three distinct points on Circle(G,s) of the same color, G has that same color.
role_in_parent: Turns three auxiliary points of color c on the small circle centered at G into the contradiction f(G)=c.
statement_nl: Let f : R^2 -> {red,green} be a coloring with the following property: for every noncollinear triple A,B,C in R^2, if f(A)=f(B)=f(C), then f(circumcenter(A,B,C))=f(A). Let G be a point of R^2 and let s>0. If X,Y,Z are three distinct points on Circle(G,s) and f(X)=f(Y)=f(Z), then f(G)=f(X).

domain_restrictions: Property P quantifies only over noncollinear triples (circumcenter is only asserted/used for noncollinear A,B,C).
s > 0 (ensures Circle(G,s) is not a single point; needed to allow three distinct points on the circle).
X, Y, Z are required distinct (explicit).
Three distinct points on a circle of positive radius are noncollinear (geometric fact used to invoke property P).
circumcenter(A,B,C) denotes the center of the unique circle through noncollinear A,B,C.
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For any function f: R^2 -> {red,green} satisfying: for all A,B,C in R^2 with A,B,C noncollinear, (f(A)=f(B)=f(C) implies f(circumcenter(A,B,C))=f(A)), the following holds: for every G in R^2 and every s>0, for every triple of distinct points X,Y,Z in R^2 with ||X-G||=||Y-G||=||Z-G||=s, if f(X)=f(Y)=f(Z) then f(G)=f(X).
quantifier_order: f : R^2 -> {red,green} (assumed to satisfy property P: for all noncollinear A,B,C in R^2, if f(A)=f(B)=f(C) then f(circumcenter(A,B,C))=f(A))
assume X, Y, Z are distinct and each lies on Circle(G,s) (i.e. ||X-G||=||Y-G||=||Z-G||=s)

witness_dependencies: circumcenter(A,B,C) exists and is well-defined only when A,B,C are noncollinear; in property P the existence is guaranteed by the noncollinearity hypothesis.

In the conclusion, because X,Y,Z are distinct points on Circle(G,s) with s>0, the circumcenter(X,Y,Z) exists and equals G. Thus the witness circumcenter(X,Y,Z) depends on the condition 'X,Y,Z lie on Circle(G,s)' and their distinctness.
No existential quantifier for f or G: f is a given coloring satisfying P and G is arbitrary; the conclusion asserts a property about this fixed f and arbitrary G,s,X,Y,Z.
